clue.text: Contented by a third moving congratulatory message

parts.note: contented means happy

indicators.note: moving the letters of 'by a third' around rearranges them

explanation.surface: Someone is pleased that a celebratory note has shifted by a third of its length.
explanation.definitionFit: A birthday greeting is the standard message of congratulation sent on someone's anniversary of birth.

clue.text: Confusion with drug he's changed for another?

definitions.note: the answer is a variant spelling of hashish, so another form of the drug in the clue

parts.note: a hash is a mess or muddle, as in 'make a hash of'
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

indicators.note: changed means the letters of he's are rearranged

explanation.surface: A muddled man has swapped one narcotic for a different one.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is the question-marked 'another': the answer is an alternative spelling of hashish, so another version of the drug just mentioned. ESH is the rearrangement of HE'S.
explanation.definitionFit: Hasheesh is a less common spelling of hashish, so it is literally another name for the cannabis resin.

clue.text: Show, one that is mounted in ancient settlement

parts.note: pomp is ceremonial show or display

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounted means the pieces are written upwards, so reversed

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, 'that is'

explanation.surface: A spectacle is staged in an old town, with one performer climbing up.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'mounted' turns I + IE upwards to give EII.
explanation.definitionFit: Pompeii was the Roman town buried by the eruption of Vesuvius in AD 79, an ancient settlement.

clue.text: Guy, so stern, upset children

indicators.note: upset means knocked over and disturbed, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A man named Guy is so severe that the kids are distressed.
explanation.definitionFit: Youngsters are young people, a general synonym for children or kids.

clue.text: See 1
Dramatist's occasionally mean after unpleasant complaint

indicators.note: after places the letters from mean behind the complaint

parts.note: IBS is irritable bowel syndrome, an unpleasant medical complaint

indicators.note: occasionally means taking only some of the letters of mean, every other one

explanation.surface: A playwright is sometimes cranky because of a nasty illness.
explanation.walkthrough: IBS, irritable bowel syndrome, is a common bowel complaint; 'occasionally' picks every other letter of 'mean'. The 's is 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Henrik Ibsen was the Norwegian playwright of A Doll's House and Hedda Gabler.

clue.text: Side of fresh meat

indicators.note: fresh suggests something made new, so the letters of meat are made into a new word

explanation.surface: A side of meat, recently butchered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Side of meat' looks like a butcher's cut, but 'Side' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: In sport a side is a team, the group of players on one side of the contest.

clue.text: Hopelessness of French prince's autobiography reported

parts.note: de is French for of

indicators.note: reported means as heard, so we take the sound of the book's title, not its spelling

parts.note: Spare is the 2023 memoir of Prince Harry

explanation.surface: A French prince's memoir is said to be full of despondency.
explanation.walkthrough: The prince is Harry, Duke of Sussex, whose 2023 memoir Spare became a bestseller.
explanation.definitionFit: Despair is the complete loss of hope, so it is a direct synonym of hopelessness.

clue.text: Long story about end of marriage

indicators.note: about means around, so the story surrounds the letter

parts.note: a yarn is a tall tale or story

indicators.note: end of takes the final letter of marriage

explanation.surface: A lengthy tale about the breakdown of a marriage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Long' looks like an adjective describing the story, but it is the verb meaning to crave.
explanation.definitionFit: To long for something is to want it intensely, which is to yearn for it.

clue.text: Without transport, touring Spain is irresponsible

indicators.note: touring means travelling round, so the first word goes round the letter

parts.note: carless means without a car, so without transport
E is the international vehicle registration code for Spain

explanation.surface: Travelling around Spain without a car would be reckless.
explanation.definitionFit: Careless conduct shows no thought for consequences, as an irresponsible person does.

clue.text: While holding baby, mother knocked back liqueur

indicators.note: knocked back means the whole is read backwards, with a nod to downing a drink
holding means the first word contains the others

parts.note: as can mean while: 'as I was leaving'
a cub is a baby animal
ma is an informal word for mother

explanation.surface: A mother with a baby in her arms gulps down a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: AS holding CUB + MA gives ACUBMAS; 'knocked back' reverses it.
explanation.definitionFit: Sambuca is an anise-flavoured Italian liqueur, often served with coffee beans.

clue.text: Birds close to shore first to approach city

parts.note: swans are birds

indicators.note: close to means the last letter of shore
first to means the opening letter of approach

explanation.surface: Birds near the coast are the first to come in.
explanation.definitionFit: Swansea is a coastal city in south Wales, the country's second largest.

clue.text: Trees, always small, covering part of golf course

indicators.note: covering means these letters go around the golf term

parts.note: ever means always, as in 'ever ready'
S is the clothing-size abbreviation for small
the green is the area of short grass round each hole

explanation.surface: Trees that are always small grow over part of a golf course.
explanation.definitionFit: Evergreens are trees and shrubs that keep their leaves all year, such as pines and hollies.

clue.text: First shock for the audience

indicators.note: for the audience means as heard by listeners, a homophone

parts.note: a shock of hair is a mane

explanation.surface: The opening surprise was staged to thrill the spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shock' looks like a surprise, but it is a thick mass of hair.
explanation.definitionFit: Main means chief or principal, as in the main event, which is the first in importance.

clue.text: A pair point out ghost

indicators.note: out means put out of order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Two people indicate that they have seen a spectre.
explanation.definitionFit: An apparition is a supernatural appearance, typically a spectre or ghost.

clue.text: Island capital protester damaged with paint

indicators.note: damaged means broken up, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A demonstrator has defaced something with paint in a seat of island government.
explanation.walkthrough: St Peter Port is the capital of Guernsey, one of the Channel Islands.
explanation.definitionFit: St Peter Port is the chief town and seat of government of the island of Guernsey.

clue.text: A German mug? Anything but!

definitions.note: a mug is also a fool, and the famous physicist was anything but a fool

parts.note: ein is German for a
a stein is a large German beer mug

explanation.surface: Is this a German beer mug? Far from it!
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mug' is both a beer stein and a slang word for a fool; the definition says the answer is the opposite of a fool.
explanation.definitionFit: Albert Einstein is the byword for a genius, the very opposite of a mug or dupe.

clue.text: Blokes curse their clothing?

definitions.note: their refers back to blokes, so the definition is men's clothing

parts.note: blokes is British slang for men
to curse is to swear

explanation.surface: Do men swear at the clothes they have to wear?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Their' points back to 'Blokes', so the definition is the clothing men wear.
explanation.definitionFit: Menswear is the retail term for clothes made and sold for men.

clue.text: Typical salesperson

definitions.meaning: first meaning: ... as an adjective, characteristic of a group
second meaning: a sales rep, who travels selling a firm's goods

explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means characteristic of a class; the noun is a firm's agent who sells its products to customers.

clue.text: Stylish creature finally leaving for pub

indicators.note: for means one thing takes the place of another, here the pub letters are swapped out

parts.note: an elephant is a creature
PH is the map abbreviation for public house

indicators.note: finally means the last letter of leaving

explanation.surface: A smart animal finally sets off for the pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'For' means 'in place of': the last letter of 'leaving', G, replaces PH in ELEPHANT.
explanation.definitionFit: Elegant means graceful and refined in appearance, so it is a synonym of stylish.

clue.text: Right to block deal in new country

indicators.note: to block means R sits inside the other letters, like an obstruction
new means the letters of deal in are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A right-wing party aims to obstruct a deal in a newly formed country.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is part of the fodder: DEAL IN rearranged by 'new' gives IELAND, and R goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Ireland is a country, both the island and the independent Republic occupying most of it.

clue.text: Building houses? He demolished houses

indicators.note: houses says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A builder asks whether a man knocked down homes.
explanation.walkthrough: The first 'houses' is part of the hidden run; the second one is the instruction that the words contain the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A shed is a simple outbuilding, used for storage or work, so it is a type of building.

clue.text: Only about five work out

indicators.note: about means around, so sole goes round the numeral

parts.note: sole means only, as in the sole survivor
V is the Roman numeral five

explanation.surface: Only around five people manage to figure it out.
explanation.definitionFit: To solve a problem is to find its answer, which is to work it out.

clue.text: People keeping dry sat in bars working, drinking last of coffee

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the rearranged letters contain the extra one
working means the letters are worked over into a new order
last of means the final letter of coffee

explanation.surface: Teetotallers sat in bars sipping coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: SAT IN BARS rearranged round E gives the answer; 'dry' means not drinking alcohol.
explanation.definitionFit: Abstainers refrain from alcohol, so they are people who stay dry, in the teetotal sense.

clue.text: Move most of funds

indicators.note: most of means the last letter is dropped

parts.note: a budget is a fund of money allotted for something

explanation.surface: A financial move involving the bulk of the money.
explanation.definitionFit: To budge is to shift position slightly, so it is a synonym of move.

clue.text: Guaranteed to keep stake

indicators.note: to keep means the first word holds the answer within its letters

explanation.surface: A sure thing worth keeping a bet on.
explanation.definitionFit: In poker the ante is the stake each player puts into the pot before the deal.

clue.text: Erudite student made money

parts.note: L is a learner, from the L-plates of a learner driver
earned means made money

explanation.surface: A scholarly student has made money.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a learner driver displays an L-plate, hence L for a student.
explanation.definitionFit: Learned (two syllables) means having much knowledge from study, a synonym of erudite.

clue.text: Copy current technology found in China

parts.note: I is the symbol for electric current

indicators.note: found in means the technology letters are placed inside the friend

parts.note: china is rhyming slang: china plate means mate
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A copy of modern technology turned up in China.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' looks like the country, but in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate, a friend.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate is to copy someone's behaviour or work, so it is a synonym.

clue.text: Highly rated opponents abounded

parts.note: in bridge East and South sit on opposing sides, so E and S are opponents
teemed means was full of or abounded

explanation.surface: Opponents who were held in high regard were everywhere.
explanation.walkthrough: Bridge is played by two pairs, North-South against East-West, so East and South oppose each other.
explanation.definitionFit: Esteemed means respected and admired, which is to be highly rated.

clue.text: Time close for Spooner's lowest point

indicators.note: Spooner's version swaps the opening sounds of two words, as the Reverend Spooner famously did

parts.note: a day is a period of time
close means near

explanation.surface: A moment approaches for one man's worst hour.
explanation.walkthrough: DAY NEAR with its first sounds swapped becomes 'nay deer', which is said like the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The nadir is the lowest point of anything, originally the point of the sky directly below the observer.
